newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway studies possible EMU cooperation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Norway studies possible EMU cooperation - paper.

text.p: Norwegian Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg was quoted as saying on Wednesday that he was studying ways of linking the Norwegian crown to a joint Europen currency.
"We cannot decide now how Norway should best cope with the creating of a joint European currency," Stoltenberg told Norwegian tabloid Dagbladet.

"But we could do it in such a way that Norway unilaterally declared a stable, firm position towards the euro. Another option would be to consider more formalised agreements between Norway and the EU," he said.
Norway rejected membership of the EU in a 1994 referendum and thus cannot join European economic and monetary union (EMU), due to start in 1999.
Former premier Gro Harlem Brundtland has said the crown should be coupled with the single European currency to be created under EMU, but she has declined to say how.
Stoltenberg switched from the energy portfolio to the finance ministry when the new Labour government of Prime Minister Thoerbjoern Jagland took office in October.
In an interview published on Wednesday with Swedish financial newspaper FinansTidningen, Stoltenberg said he could envisage co-operation between Norway and EMU.
"I am for monetary union because it will lead to currency stability in Europe," Stoltenberg was quoted as saying by the Swedish newspaper.
"I can see co-operation with the future euro bloc," said Stoltenberg.
Norway has a managed float for the crown and its central bank seeks to maintain a stable exchange rate against European currencies.
However, the Norwegian crown has rocketed to 52-month highs against the German mark since December on the back of the strong oil-driven Norwegian economy.
